files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close — controller's checklist

Owner: L. Mbeki. Complete in sequence; no shortcuts.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, prepare one correcting journal entry per item.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 and paying in July. If one exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities; note that in some months every payroll run pays in-month.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule and supporting contracts. Check the GL first to avoid a duplicate. If the entry is missing, book June amortization as ONE combined journal entry. Apply the convention that a full month is taken in the month an item begins.
4. Book June depreciation per the fixed asset register, after verifying the GL does not already contain the entry.
5. Compare June vendor-bill documents with GL coding. Verify each expense account and reclass anything miscoded.
6. Prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis, after items 1-5 have been booked.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Quartz Relay Inc. began in 2021 after its founders spent too many late evenings tracing customer notifications across disconnected tools. They built a lightweight relay layer that gave operations teams one place to design, route, monitor, and troubleshoot automated messages without replacing the systems already in use.

Today, Quartz Relay Inc. sells cloud software for dependable event delivery and workflow communication. Customers use the platform to move alerts, status updates, and other operational messages between internal applications and customer-facing channels. The product is deliberately practical: clear logs, sensible controls, and support from people who understand how messy production systems can become.

The team has the flavor of a small, experienced SaaS shop. Engineers sit close to customer support, product discussions often start with a real ticket, and sales favors useful demonstrations over polished theater. Finance and operations remain lean, with staff wearing several hats and documenting processes as the company grows.

The current focus is steady execution: improving delivery visibility, simplifying onboarding, and building stronger partnerships with adjacent software providers. Leadership is also sharpening the company’s positioning so prospects understand that Quartz is not another messaging channel; it is the connective layer that helps existing channels work reliably.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## What we want to accomplish

- Refresh the Quartz Relay Inc. story around reliable workflow communication, not generic messaging.
- Give operations and engineering buyers clearer examples of where the platform fits.
- Build a repeatable partner co-marketing motion without creating a heavy program.
- Turn customer questions into useful educational content for prospects.

## Core programs

### Brand and website
Tighten the homepage narrative, simplify product language, and replace broad claims with concrete use cases. Keep the visual refresh light enough that the team can ship it without distracting from product work.

### Webinars
Run two practical sessions per quarter. Favor live product walkthroughs, troubleshooting clinics, and conversations with operators over formal slide presentations. Reuse each session as short clips, an article, and sales follow-up material.

### Partner pilot
Select a small group of complementary software providers for shared guides, guest sessions, and mutual introductions. Start hands-on; document what works before turning it into a formal playbook.

### Customer proof
Develop concise stories focused on implementation, day-to-day operations, and measurable workflow improvements. Obtain approval early and offer anonymous formats where needed.

## Quarter emphasis

- Q3: messaging refresh, first webinar cycle, partner outreach, and content inventory.
- Q4: publish customer proof, expand the strongest partner activity, and refine webinar topics from audience feedback.

## Open items

Confirm owners, production capacity, channel mix, and success measures after the Q2 close.
files.notes/prior_accountant_memo.md:
# Handoff notes from your chatty predecessor

For L. Mbeki — a few things that are easy to miss:

- The bank likes to tuck its own fees and charges near the end of the statement. We book those at close rather than during the month, so do not assume the ledger already has them.
- Give the June vendor bills a careful coding pass. A couple may have gone to the wrong expense account, and the documents in `bills/` are authoritative if the GL description tells a different story.
- The Q2 budget was fixed in early April. The one-off items that arrived in June were never planned, and they are the reason the large variances look large.
- Payroll timing matters this month: the back half of June pays out in early July. The payroll register has the dates, so use that rather than guessing.
